# A test waiting on a timer sees it tick, on every target: one in a `for` in
# a tab's panel, and a component's own beside it, whose count is a cell per
# copy on bubbletea and an instance's own state on android.
#
# bubbletea's test build ran no command the Model asked for -- its schedules
# are tea.Tick commands Init and Update return, and a test calls the Model's
# methods with no program running them -- so no timer ever ticked under a
# test, in a tab or out. A waiting test settles the Model it holds each turn
# now: Update after what the test did, its commands run off the test's
# goroutine and their messages posted back to be delivered on it
# (codegen/platform/bubbletea/post.go).
#
# android's test runner lowered no t.wait at all; it moves Compose's test
# clock on while it asks the predicate. And android hoisted every timer to
# the top of the screen, which dropped one under a loop -- it has none of the
# loop's variables to read there -- and put one an instance renders in the
# screen, naming the instance's state from outside it. Each is rendered where
# it was written now, as the LaunchedEffect it is.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component spinner ui.node {
    var n = 0
    time.timer(interval=20ms, @tick {
        n += 1
    })
    ui.text(value="{n}")
}

component main ui.node {
    var idx = 0
    var ticks = [0, 0]
    var rows = [1, 2]
    ui.tabs(:selected=idx) {
        ui.tab(label="One") {
            for var i, n = ticks {
                time.timer(interval=20ms, @tick {
                    ticks[i] = ticks[i] + 1
                })
                ui.text(value="{n}")
            }
            for var r = rows {
                spinner #s()
            }
        }
        ui.tab(label="Two") {
            ui.text(value="two")
        }
    }
}

func testATimerInATabsLoopTicks(t Test, c main) {
    t.wait(func() => c.ticks[0] > 1 && c.ticks[1] > 1, 3000)
    t.assert(c.ticks[0] > 1 && c.ticks[1] > 1)
}

func testAStatefulTimerInATabsLoopTicks(t Test, c main) {
    t.wait(func() => c.s[0].n > 1 && c.s[1].n > 1, 3000)
    t.assert(c.s[0].n > 1 && c.s[1].n > 1)
}

ui.window {
    main
}
